title: Bolder hand: choose the visual world
question: Bolder register. The deal leads with the Collider Event Display. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.thesis: One prompt enters at the centre of a detector; its tracks curve out through the rings (build, test, deploy) and land as a product. The workshop is the collision.
materials: curved particle tracks in Paytm sky and signal yellow
options.viewport: A full-viewport event display on the right: rings drawn in SVG and canvas, tracks that animate out from the beamline and label themselves (Suman Mandal · Paytm, Shivam Behl · Microsoft, 30 SEP, SEMINAR HALL). On the left, a readout column: PROMPT → PRODUCTION, NBKRIST × ISTE × Paytm, date, time, venue and fee as run parameters, and a big REGISTER trigger. The official poster sits in the first calorimeter wedge as a detail view.
options.risk: Dark ground plus bright accents can slide into generic 'neon tech'; the rings, tracks and readouts must stay rigorously scientific, and forms/dashboards go light-surfaced for legibility.

raised.raise: Readouts use one strict monospace digit grid for every number: countdown, seats, fees, ticket IDs, scores.
Colour is rationed: Paytm sky marks only the live/active track, yellow only a selected item, red only energy/alerts; steel-navy holds everything else.
One axis rules each page: the day's schedule runs as a single radial time axis from 9:00 to 16:00, not a stack of cards.
Every ticket, submission and certificate carries a small origin tag (ID, time, source) like a reconstructed event record.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: The whole site is a live monospace render: the poster, speakers and QR re-drawn in glyph density.
options.viewport: The speakers' portraits rendered live in ASCII glyphs that sharpen into photos on hover; the event facts sit in the same grid as terminal output.
options.case: CS students identify with it instantly, but the monospace-everything grid is harder to read for faculty and long forms.
options.risk: Reads as a hacker costume rather than an official institute event.

options.label: Rietveld Sliding Planes
options.thesis: One page of sliding planes: register, schedule and speakers slide into the same room.
options.viewport: An asymmetric grid of planes with the poster as one plane; clicking Schedule slides a plane across to reveal the timeline.
options.case: Very clear for forms, admin and dashboards; weaker link to AI, Paytm or the campus.
options.risk: Reads like an art-school exercise rather than an AI workshop.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: The day as a descent, one vertical depth axis.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile as the schedule.
options.case: No connection to the audience or subject.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Stalls trading shadows, each tagged with an origin ticket.
options.case: Surreal and off-brand for an institute + Paytm event.
options.kept: Every item carries a small origin ticket.

options.label: Flash-Scrawl Club Sleeve
options.thesis: Flash photo defaced with marker and a sticker.
options.viewport: Scrawled logo over a flash photo.
options.case: No real event photos exist, and it's the wrong register for an official event.
options.kept: Completed steps stay marked on the surface as history.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean university/tech event site, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Poster and event facts side by side, a clear Register button, then speakers and schedule.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other college event page.
